subject: Taxation
chapterTitle: Tax Deduction at Source and Collection of Tax at Source

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Under Section 51 of the CGST Act, 2017, who among the following is NOT required to deduct Tax at Source (TDS)?
options: A department or establishment of the Central Government
A local authority whose total annual turnover in the preceding financial year was Rs. 25 Lakhs
An authority or a board set up by Parliament with 51% or more participation by Government
A society established by the Central Government or a State Government with 100% control
plain.explanation: Section 51 mandates TDS for departments of Central/State Government, local authorities, governmental agencies, and societies owned/controlled by the Government. The turnover threshold of the local authority does not exempt them from TDS liability if they fall under the specified categories of deductors, making local authorities universally subject to TDS regardless of turnover.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Tax Deduction at Source and Collection of Tax at Source

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: What is the rate of Tax Deduction at Source (TDS) under the CGST Act, 2017?
plain.explanation: As per Section 51(1) of the CGST Act, 2017 read with relevant notifications, TDS is required to be deducted at the rate of 1% under CGST and 1% under SGST/UTGST (or 2% under IGST) of the payment made or credited to the supplier.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Tax Deduction at Source and Collection of Tax at Source

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: TDS under Section 51 of the CGST Act is applicable when the total value of supply under a contract exceeds which of the following limits?
plain.explanation: As per the proviso to Section 51(1) of the CGST Act, 2017, TDS is to be deducted only if the total value of supply under a single contract, excluding the tax components, exceeds Rs. 2,50,000.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Tax Deduction at Source and Collection of Tax at Source

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: In computing the contract value of Rs. 2,50,000 for the purpose of TDS deduction under Section 51, which of the following elements must be excluded?
options: Central Tax, State Tax, Integrated Tax, and Cess
Incidental expenses charged by the supplier
plain.explanation: The threshold of Rs. 2,50,000 for TDS under Section 51 is evaluated based on the contract value excluding the taxes leviable under CGST, SGST, UTGST, IGST, and GST Compensation Cess.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Tax Deduction at Source and Collection of Tax at Source

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Within how many days from the end of the month in which TDS is deducted must the deductor deposit the amount to the government account?
plain.explanation: Under Section 51(3) of the CGST Act, 2017, the amount deducted as TDS must be paid to the government by the deductor within 10 days after the end of the month in which the deduction was made.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Tax Deduction at Source and Collection of Tax at Source

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Which form is required to be issued by the deductor to the deductee detailing the TDS deducted and deposited?
plain.explanation: As per Rule 66(3) of the CGST Rules, 2017, the certificate of TDS deduction in Form GSTR-7A must be issued by the deductor to the deductee within 5 days of crediting the amount to the Government.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Tax Deduction at Source and Collection of Tax at Source

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: What is the consequence if a deductor fails to furnish the TDS certificate (Form GSTR-7A) within the stipulated time of 5 days of crediting the amount to the government?
options: Late fee of Rs. 100 per day up to a maximum of Rs. 5,000
Late fee of Rs. 50 per day up to a maximum of Rs. 2,000
Penal interest of 18% per annum only
No late fee is prescribed under GST law for GSTR-7A delay
plain.explanation: Section 51(4) read with Section 47 prescribes a late fee of Rs. 100 per day for each day during which the failure continues, subject to a maximum of Rs. 5,000, for failure to furnish the TDS certificate in Form GSTR-7A.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Tax Deduction at Source and Collection of Tax at Source

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: If a deductor fails to deposit the deducted TDS to the Government account within the due date, what interest rate is payable by the deductor?
plain.explanation: As per Section 51(6) read with Section 50, if any deductor fails to pay to the Government the amount deducted as TDS, they shall pay interest at the rate of 18% per annum for the period for which the failure continues.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Tax Deduction at Source and Collection of Tax at Source

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Which return must be filed by a registered person who is required to deduct Tax at Source under Section 51?
plain.explanation: Form GSTR-7 is the monthly return required to be filed by persons who are required to deduct Tax at Source under Section 51 of the CGST Act, 2017, on or before the 10th day of the month succeeding the calendar month.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Tax Deduction at Source and Collection of Tax at Source

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Under Section 52 of the CGST Act, 2017, 'Tax Collection at Source' (TCS) is applicable to which of the following entities?
options: Any registered supplier selling goods online
Only foreign e-commerce operators operating in India
Every supplier who has a turnover exceeding Rs. 20 Lakhs
plain.explanation: Section 52 of the CGST Act, 2017 mandates every electronic commerce operator (ECO) to collect an amount known as Tax Collection at Source (TCS) out of the net value of taxable supplies made through it by other suppliers where the consideration is to be collected by the ECO.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Tax Deduction at Source and Collection of Tax at Source

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: What is the standard total rate of Tax Collection at Source (TCS) required to be collected by an e-commerce operator under Section 52?
plain.explanation: As per Section 52(1) of the CGST Act, 2017, an ECO is required to collect TCS at such rate not exceeding 1% (0.5% CGST and 0.5% SGST/UTGST) of the net value of taxable supplies made through it.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Tax Deduction at Source and Collection of Tax at Source

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: What is the definition of 'net value of taxable supplies' for the purpose of calculating TCS under Section 52?
options: Total gross sales of goods and services through the ECO
Aggregate value of taxable supplies of goods or services made during any month less the value of supplies returned
Total invoice value including all taxes
Gross collections made by the ECO minus its own commission
plain.explanation: Section 52(1) defines 'net value of taxable supplies' as the aggregate value of taxable supplies of goods or services, other than services notified under Section 9(5), made during any month by all registered persons through the operator reduced by the aggregate value of taxable supplies returned to the suppliers during the said month.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Tax Deduction at Source and Collection of Tax at Source

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Within what period must an e-commerce operator deposit the collected TCS into the Government account?
options: Within 7 days after the end of the month
Within 10 days after the end of the month
Within 14 days after the end of the month
Within 20 days after the end of the month
plain.explanation: Under Section 52(3) of the CGST Act, 2017, the amount collected as TCS must be paid to the government by the operator within 10 days after the end of the calendar month in which collection was made.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Tax Deduction at Source and Collection of Tax at Source

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Which monthly return must be filed by an e-commerce operator containing details of outward supplies, returns, and TCS collected?
plain.explanation: As per Section 52(4), every electronic commerce operator is required to furnish a statement in Form GSTR-8 electronically on or before the 10th day of the month succeeding the calendar month in which TCS was collected.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Tax Deduction at Source and Collection of Tax at Source

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: What annual statement must an e-commerce operator file detailing supplies effected and TCS collected during the financial year?
plain.explanation: Under Section 52(5) of the CGST Act, 2017, every ECO must furnish an annual statement in Form GSTR-9B electronically on or before the 31st day of December following the end of the financial year to which such statement relates.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Tax Deduction at Source and Collection of Tax at Source

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: If a notice is issued by a proper officer to an e-commerce operator requiring information regarding supplies made through it, within how many days must the operator furnish such information?
plain.explanation: Section 52(12) states that any person to whom a notice is issued under Section 52(11) to furnish information shall furnish such information within 15 working days from the date of service of such notice.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Tax Deduction at Source and Collection of Tax at Source

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Where does the amount of TCS deducted/collected by an e-commerce operator reflect for the supplier of goods or services?
plain.explanation: As per Section 52(7) of the CGST Act, 2017, the details of TCS furnished by an operator in GSTR-8 shall be made available to each of the suppliers in Part C of Form GSTR-2A/electronic cash ledger upon validation, and the amount collected is credited to the electronic cash ledger of the respective supplier.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Tax Deduction at Source and Collection of Tax at Source

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Who is exempted from the requirement of compulsory registration even if they make supplies through an electronic commerce operator, as per recent GST council relaxations/provisions?
options: Suppliers of all types of goods
Persons making intra-state supplies through ECO having aggregate turnover below threshold
Suppliers of services making supplies through ECO
No supplier is exempted from registration if supplying through ECO
plain.explanation: As per specific notifications issued under Section 24(ix) read with Section 9(5), certain categories of persons making supplies of goods or services through an ECO can be exempt from compulsory registration provided their aggregate turnover does not exceed the threshold limit, subject to specific conditions.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Tax Deduction at Source and Collection of Tax at Source

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Can a deductor under Section 51 claim refund of TDS deducted and deposited by him in excess of the actual tax liability?
options: Yes, the deductor can claim refund directly.
No, refund can only be claimed by the deductee if the amount has been credited to their electronic cash ledger.
Yes, after getting a no-objection certificate from the supplier.
No refund is ever allowed for TDS under GST.
plain.explanation: As per the statutory provisions, any excess TDS deducted and deposited can generally be claimed as a refund by the deductee once it is credited to their electronic cash ledger, subject to the conditions specified under Section 54.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Tax Deduction at Source and Collection of Tax at Source

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: In case supplies are made through an ECO where tax is payable by the ECO under Section 9(5) (e.g., passenger transport services through aggregator), is TCS required to be collected under Section 52?
options: Yes, TCS must be collected in all cases.
No, TCS is not required to be collected on supplies where ECO is liable to pay tax under Section 9(5).
TCS is collected at a reduced rate of 0.1%.
TCS is optional for supplies under Section 9(5).
plain.explanation: Section 52(1) explicitly excludes services notified under Section 9(5) from the net value of taxable supplies for the purpose of TCS calculation, as the ECO is directly liable to pay tax on such supplies under Section 9(5).

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Tax Deduction at Source and Collection of Tax at Source

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: What happens if a deductor under Section 51 deducts TDS but fails to deposit it along with applicable interest? Can the deductee take credit of such un-deposited TDS?
options: No, credit in the electronic cash ledger reflects only when the deducted amount is actually credited to the Government account by the deductor.
Yes, if the deductee produces an indemnity bond.
Credit is given conditionally for 30 days.
plain.explanation: The credit of TDS deducted is reflected in the electronic cash ledger of the deductee only after the deductor files GSTR-7 and deposits the amount into the Government treasury.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Tax Deduction at Source and Collection of Tax at Source

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Which of the following persons is mandatorily required to obtain registration under Section 24 of the CGST Act solely due to e-commerce participation?
options: Every person supplying goods through an electronic commerce operator who is required to collect tax under section 52
Every person supplying services through any website
Every person having a turnover of Rs. 10 Lakhs
Every supplier of exempted goods via e-commerce
plain.explanation: As per Section 24(ix) of the CGST Act, 2017, persons who supply goods or services through an electronic commerce operator who is required to collect tax under section 52 are required to obtain compulsory registration, subject to threshold exemptions provided via notifications.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Tax Deduction at Source and Collection of Tax at Source

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: What is the penalty for failure to furnish the annual statement in GSTR-9B by an e-commerce operator within the due date?
options: Rs. 100 per day under CGST and Rs. 100 per day under SGST, subject to a maximum of 0.25% of turnover in the State/UT
No penalty is specified for GSTR-9B
Cancellation of registration immediately without notice
plain.explanation: Section 47(2) provides that any registered person who fails to furnish the annual return/statement under Section 44 (which includes GSTR-9B) by the due date shall pay a late fee of Rs. 100 for every day during which such failure continues, subject to a maximum of an amount calculated at 0.25% of turnover in the State/UT.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Tax Deduction at Source and Collection of Tax at Source

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: If a contract has a total value of Rs. 3,00,000 inclusive of CGST and SGST of Rs. 36,000 (i.e. basic value Rs. 2,64,000), will TDS be deducted under Section 51?
options: No, because the total invoice value is considered.
Yes, because the contract value excluding taxes (Rs. 2,64,000) exceeds Rs. 2,50,000.
No, because the basic value must exceed Rs. 3,00,000.
Yes, because any contract above Rs. 2,00,000 is subject to TDS.
plain.explanation: The threshold for TDS under Section 51 is Rs. 2,50,000 of the contract value excluding Central tax, State tax, Integrated tax, and Cess. Here, the basic contract value is Rs. 2,64,000, which exceeds Rs. 2,50,000, hence TDS is applicable.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Tax Deduction at Source and Collection of Tax at Source

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Can a government department acting as a deductor under Section 51 obtain a separate registration for TDS without holding a regular GSTIN as a supplier?
options: No, they must obtain regular registration as a normal taxpayer.
Yes, deductors can obtain a distinct registration dedicated solely to TDS/TCS collection.
Registration is not required at all for government departments.
They must use the PAN of the state treasury.
plain.explanation: As per Section 24(vi) read with the registration rules, persons required to deduct tax under Section 51 or collect tax under Section 52 must obtain a separate registration (TAN-like GST registration) specifically for TDS/TCS operations.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Tax Deduction at Source and Collection of Tax at Source

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: What is the due date for filing the monthly return in Form GSTR-7 by a TDS deductor?
plain.explanation: Rule 66 of the CGST Rules, 2017 prescribes that every registered person required to deduct TDS shall furnish a return in Form GSTR-7 electronically for the month in which deduction was made, on or before the 10th day of the succeeding month.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Tax Deduction at Source and Collection of Tax at Source

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Which of the following transactions is exempt from TDS under Section 51 of the CGST Act?
options: Supply of taxable goods made by a supplier to a Central Government department under a contract worth Rs. 3,00,000.
Supply of goods or services where both the supplier and the recipient deductor are located in the same State.
Supply of goods or services where the location of the supplier and the place of supply is in a State/UT different from the registration of the recipient deductor.
Supply of taxable services worth Rs. 5,00,000 to a local authority.
plain.explanation: As per the proviso to Section 51(1), no TDS is required to be deducted where the location of the supplier and the place of supply is in a State/UT different from the State/UT of registration of the recipient.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Tax Deduction at Source and Collection of Tax at Source

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: An electronic commerce operator fails to submit matching corrections for discrepancies pointed out in GSTR-8 within the specified time. What is the statutory implication?
options: The discrepancy is added to the output tax liability of the ECO.
The supply value in discrepancy is added to the output tax liability of the supplier along with interest.
plain.explanation: Section 52(9) and (10) provide that details of supplies furnished by the operator and those furnished by the supplier in their returns are matched, and any discrepancy not communicated/rectified results in the amount being added to the output tax liability of the supplier.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Tax Deduction at Source and Collection of Tax at Source

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: If a deductor fails to deduct TDS under Section 51, is the deductor liable to pay interest and penalty even if the supplier has paid the full tax on the transaction?
options: Yes, the statutory obligation to deduct and deposit TDS is independent, and failure attracts interest under Section 50 and penalties.
No, if the supplier pays tax, the deductor is fully absolved.
Penalty is levied only on the supplier.
plain.explanation: The obligation to deduct TDS under Section 51 is a statutory duty cast upon the deductor. Failure to deduct or deposit attracts interest and penalties irrespective of whether the supplier has discharged their tax liability.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Tax Deduction at Source and Collection of Tax at Source

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Under Section 52(11), an officer not below the rank of which of the following may empower any officer to audit or inspect an e-commerce operator?
plain.explanation: As per Section 52(11) of the CGST Act, 2017, any authority not below the rank of Commissioner may serve notice on an e-commerce operator to furnish details relating to volume of goods/services supplied, stock turnover, etc.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Tax Deduction at Source and Collection of Tax at Source

scenarios.subject: Taxation
scenarios.passage: M/s Alpha Builders, a registered partnership firm in Maharashtra, enters into a works contract with the Public Works Department (PWD) of the Government of Maharashtra, located in Mumbai. The total contract value is fixed at Rs. 4,00,000 (excluding CGST and SGST at 9% each). Both the supplier and the PWD are in Maharashtra, and the place of supply is also Maharashtra. PWD credits the running bill of Rs. 3,00,000 (excluding taxes) to Alpha Builders on 15th October 2026.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Tax Deduction at Source and Collection of Tax at Source

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Is PWD Maharashtra required to deduct Tax at Source (TDS) on the payment made to M/s Alpha Builders?
options: No, because PWD is a government body and exempt from TDS.
Yes, because PWD is a Government department, the contract value exceeds Rs. 2,50,000, and both parties are in the same State.
No, because works contracts are completely excluded from TDS.
Yes, but only if Alpha Builders turnover exceeds Rs. 40 Lakhs.
linkedMcqs.explanation: PWD is a department of the State Government, making it a mandatory deductor under Section 51. The basic contract value (Rs. 4,00,000) exceeds the threshold of Rs. 2,50,000, and the location of supplier, place of supply, and recipient are in the same State (Maharashtra), satisfying all conditions for TDS.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the exact amount of TDS that PWD Maharashtra must deduct from the running bill of Rs. 3,00,000?
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under Section 51, TDS is deducted at 1% CGST and 1% SGST of the payment made. For a payment of Rs. 3,00,000, 1% CGST equals Rs. 3,000 and 1% SGST equals Rs. 3,000.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: By what date must PWD Maharashtra deposit the deducted TDS amount to the Government account?
linkedMcqs.explanation: As per Section 51(3), the TDS deducted during October 2026 must be paid to the government by the deductor within 10 days after the end of the month, i.e., on or before 10th November 2026.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Which return must PWD Maharashtra file to report this TDS deduction?
linkedMcqs.explanation: Form GSTR-7 is the prescribed monthly return under Rule 66 to be filed by deductors registered under Section 51 for reporting tax deducted at source.

scenarios.subject: Taxation
scenarios.passage: M/s QuickShop, an electronic commerce operator (ECO) based in Delhi, operates an online marketplace. During the month of August 2026, various registered suppliers sell goods through QuickShop. The gross value of taxable supplies made through QuickShop is Rs. 50,00,000. During the same month, goods amounting to Rs. 5,00,000 are returned by customers. QuickShop collects the consideration on behalf of the suppliers.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Tax Deduction at Source and Collection of Tax at Source

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the net value of taxable supplies for QuickShop for the month of August 2026 for the purpose of TCS?
linkedMcqs.explanation: Net value of taxable supplies under Section 52(1) is the aggregate value of taxable supplies made through the operator reduced by the aggregate value of taxable supplies returned during the month (Rs. 50,00,000 - Rs. 5,00,000 = Rs. 45,00,000).

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the total TCS amount that QuickShop is required to collect for August 2026?
linkedMcqs.explanation: TCS is collected at 1% of the net value of taxable supplies (0.5% CGST + 0.5% SGST, or 1% IGST). 1% of Rs. 45,00,000 equals Rs. 45,000.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: By what date must QuickShop file its monthly statement in Form GSTR-8 for August 2026?
linkedMcqs.explanation: As per Section 52(4), Form GSTR-8 must be filed electronically by the e-commerce operator on or before the 10th day of the month succeeding the calendar month in which TCS was collected, i.e., 10th September 2026.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Where will the TCS collected by QuickShop reflect for the registered suppliers selling through QuickShop?
linkedMcqs.explanation: As per Section 52(7), the TCS amount collected by the ECO is credited to the electronic cash ledger of the respective supplier upon validation of details furnished in GSTR-8.

scenarios.subject: Taxation
scenarios.passage: M/s Apex Infotech, a registered software supplier in Karnataka, enters into a contract worth Rs. 5,00,000 with a Central Government PSU located in Chennai, Tamil Nadu, to supply customized software. The place of supply of software is determined to be Chennai, Tamil Nadu (location of the recipient PSU). Apex Infotech fulfills the order and the PSU makes a payment of Rs. 4,00,000 on 1st November 2026.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Tax Deduction at Source and Collection of Tax at Source

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Is the Central Government PSU required to deduct TDS under Section 51 in this transaction?
options: Yes, because the PSU is a government-controlled entity and contract value exceeds Rs. 2,50,000.
No, because the location of the supplier (Karnataka) and the place of supply / recipient registration state (Tamil Nadu) are different.
No, because software supplies are exempt from TDS.
Yes, at the rate of 2% CGST and 2% SGST.
linkedMcqs.explanation: The proviso to Section 51(1) clearly specifies that no TDS shall be deducted if the location of the supplier and the place of supply is in a State/UT different from the State/UT of registration of the recipient. Here, supplier is in Karnataka and place of supply is Tamil Nadu.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What would be the outcome if both Apex Infotech and the PSU were located in Chennai, Tamil Nadu, with the place of supply also in Tamil Nadu?
options: TDS would still not be applicable.
TDS would be mandatory as all conditions under Section 51 would be met.
TCS would apply instead of TDS.
linkedMcqs.explanation: If the supplier, place of supply, and recipient deductor are all in the same State (Tamil Nadu), and the contract value exceeds Rs. 2,50,000, TDS deduction under Section 51 is mandatory.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: If TDS was applicable in this transaction, what would be the IGST rate of TDS to be deducted?
linkedMcqs.explanation: For an inter-state supply where TDS is applicable, the rate of TDS under IGST is 2% (1% CGST + 1% SGST equivalent).

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Who is responsible for verifying the contract value threshold for TDS under Section 51?
linkedMcqs.explanation: The statutory responsibility to check whether the contract value exceeds Rs. 2,50,000 and to deduct TDS lies with the deductor at the time of making payment or credit.

scenarios.subject: Taxation
scenarios.passage: M/s ZoomCab Services, an aggregator operating in West Bengal, provides passenger transport services through its mobile application. During September 2026, individual cab drivers registered on ZoomCab provided transport services through the app, generating a gross collection of Rs. 20,00,000. Under GST law, passenger transport services provided through an electronic commerce aggregator are notified under Section 9(5).

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Tax Deduction at Source and Collection of Tax at Source

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Is M/s ZoomCab Services required to collect Tax Collection at Source (TCS) under Section 52 on these passenger transport services?
options: No, because services notified under Section 9(5) are explicitly excluded from the net value of taxable supplies for TCS under Section 52.
No, because transport services are exempt.
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 52(1) excludes supplies notified under Section 9(5) from the net value of taxable supplies for TCS calculation because the ECO itself is liable to pay tax under Section 9(5) as if it were the supplier.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Who is liable to pay GST on the passenger transport services provided through ZoomCab aggregator?
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under Section 9(5) of the CGST Act, 2017, the electronic commerce operator is liable to pay tax on supply of services notified thereunder, such as passenger transport services provided through an aggregator.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Does ZoomCab need to file GSTR-8 in respect of supplies covered under Section 9(5)?
options: GSTR-8 is for TCS supplies; since Section 9(5) supplies are excluded from TCS, they are not reported as TCS supplies in GSTR-8.
Yes, GSTR-8 must include Section 9(5) supplies as TCS.
GSTR-8 is replaced by GSTR-3B entirely.
No GST return is required for ZoomCab.
linkedMcqs.explanation: Since Section 9(5) supplies are not subject to TCS under Section 52, they do not form part of the TCS calculations reported in GSTR-8, though the ECO pays tax on them via GSTR-3B.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: If ZoomCab also sold miscellaneous car accessories (goods) through its platform in the same month worth Rs. 2,00,000, would TCS apply to those goods?
options: No, because the transport service is exempt.
Yes, TCS under Section 52 applies to the supply of goods made through the ECO, provided they are not under Section 9(5).
TCS applies only if goods exceed Rs. 50,00,000.
Car accessories are notified under Section 9(5) as well.
linkedMcqs.explanation: TCS under Section 52 applies to taxable supplies of goods or services made through an ECO, except those covered under Section 9(5). Since car accessories are goods and not under Section 9(5), TCS applies to them.

scenarios.subject: Taxation
scenarios.passage: M/s Delta Supplies, a registered trader in Gujarat, made supplies of office stationery to a State Government educational institution in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, under a contract amounting to Rs. 3,50,000 (excluding taxes) in July 2026. The educational institution deducted TDS of 2% (1% CGST + 1% SGST) amounting to Rs. 7,000 on 10th August 2026. However, due to administrative oversight, the institution failed to deposit the deducted Rs. 7,000 into the Government account until 15th October 2026.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Tax Deduction at Source and Collection of Tax at Source

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What interest liability is attracted by the educational institution for the delayed deposit of TDS?
options: No interest if it is an educational institution
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under Section 51(6) read with Section 50, if any deductor fails to pay to the Government the amount deducted as TDS, they shall pay interest at the rate of 18% per annum for the period of delay.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: When will the TDS amount of Rs. 7,000 reflect in the electronic cash ledger of M/s Delta Supplies?
options: Immediately when TDS is deducted by the institution
Only after the institution files GSTR-7 and deposits the amount into the Government treasury
On the last day of the financial year
Never, because it is an educational institution
linkedMcqs.explanation: The credit of TDS deducted is reflected in the electronic cash ledger of the deductee only after the deductor deposits the amount and files the GSTR-7 return matching the deduction.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the due date by which the educational institution should have originally deposited the TDS deducted on 10th August 2026?
linkedMcqs.explanation: As per Section 51(3), TDS deducted during a month must be paid to the Government within 10 days after the end of that month. For August 2026, the due date is 10th September 2026.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the consequence if the educational institution fails to issue Form GSTR-7A to M/s Delta Supplies within 5 days of crediting the amount to the Government?
options: Late fee of Rs. 100 per day subject to a maximum of Rs. 5,000
linkedMcqs.explanation: As per Section 51(4) read with Section 47, failure to furnish the TDS certificate in Form GSTR-7A within 5 days attracts a late fee of Rs. 100 per day up to a maximum of Rs. 5,000.
